is: One module per `POST /api/<control>`: each takes a JSON body naming a project of the zaf home's list, calls the app function the matching verb calls from that project's root, and answers what happened or the refusal with its reason.
conventions: No body is read before the guard admits the request, and no project off the zaf home's list is ever reached
Status codes are shared: 200 done, 400 a body that is not that, 404 a project the list does not hold, 409 a refusal of the state (nothing changed), 500 a backend that failed
A control answers what the verb's --json says, plus plain words

fs.name: answer.rs
fs.role: `POST /api/answer`: the Engineer's ruling on an open question, as `zaf board ruling`

fs.name: drop.rs
fs.role: `POST /api/drop`: takes a project off the list only when its entry reads missing (503 with no zaf home); needs only the home, so it is always built

fs.name: project.rs
fs.role: what tick and watch share: the listed project a body names and the version it runs for, given or remembered on its entry

fs.name: stop.rs
fs.role: `POST /api/stop`: ends a task's running instance and releases its claim, as `zaf spawn stop`

fs.name: tests.rs
fs.role: stop, tick, drop and answer over the dashboard's socket, end to end: the guard, the project, what the control does

fs.name: tick.rs
fs.role: `POST /api/tick`: one spawner tick through the Ticker the hub was given, as `zaf spawn --once --no-wait`

fs.name: watch.rs
fs.role: `POST /api/watch`: starts or stops the project's watch inside the hub (202 for a stop whose tick still runs); a scheduler the hub did not start is never stopped

notes: The Ticker and the watch's tick are implemented in cli/hub/tick.rs and cli/hub/watch.rs, each a process of its own in the project's root
drop/, stop/, tick/ and watch/ hold only tests.rs
